newsitem.title: USA: Corporate controllers upbeat on U.S economy - survey.
newsitem.headline: Corporate controllers upbeat on U.S economy - survey.

text.p: Corporate trust in the U.S. economy has risen to its highest level in ten quarters, according to a survey of corporate controllers released on Monday.
The Controllers Confidence Index, an economic outlook of the Controllers Council of the Institute of Management Accountants, rose to 66.4 in the third quarter from 65.9 in the second quarter.
The survey of approximately 2,000 Controllers Council members received a 14 percent response rate, said an institute spokeswoman.

The improved outlook is based on controllers' positive forecasts of stable inflation and unchanged interest rates, the IMA said. Controllers expect increases in sales, profits, cash flows and corporate spending through year end and a modest economic upturn in 1997.

Specifically, 62 percent of responding controllers expect their company sales to grow an average of 17 percent in 1996, while 15 percent said sales would fall an average of 13 percent. Another 23 percent of respondents said sales would likely go unchanged for the year.

More than half of controllers surveyed expect company profits to grow by an average of 27 percent in 1996, while a quarter of respondents expect an average decline of 13 percent. Another 23 percent expect flat sales.

On the employment front, 46 percent of respondents said levels would remain unchanged while 36 percent expect an average increase in employment of 10 percent, for a total of 82 percent expecting either flat or higher employment levels for 1996.
The survey said 18 percent of respondents expected an employment shrinkage of about eight percent.

Elsewhere, 51 percent of responding controllers expect an average cash flow increase of 22 percent for 1996. Another 27 percent of respondents said cash flows will be flat and 22 percent said cash flows would decrease below 1995 levels.
The survey also said 59 percent of respondents expect an overall inflation rate of three percent and 60 percent expect short-term interest rates will be flat through the fourth quarter.
The Institute of Management Accountants is comprised of 82,000 members and is based in Montvale, New Jersey.
